title: Lumbar torso torque-angle with an abdominal belt or held breath: exponential fits in six directions, males and females
levels: lumbar (rib cage/xiphoid relative to pelvis; moment about ~L4/L5)
condition: relaxed (EMG biofeedback) with (a) breath held at maximal inhalation or (b) leather lifting belt

quantity.name: applied torque vs lumbar torso angle (belt / held breath)
quantity.definition: T = lambda*exp(beta*alpha) fitted to the mean raw data per sex, direction and condition from 0 Nm to the torque tolerated by half the subjects; T in Nm about ~L4/L5, alpha in deg; points at 5/10/15 deg derived from the fits; Table 2 lists the torque levels at which the bending angle differed significantly from the normal condition

source.authors: McGill S, Seguin J, Bennett G
source.sample: 22 male + 15 female undergraduates, no disabling LBP in the previous year

protocol.summary: Flexion/extension: side-lying; lateral bend: supine. Pelvis and lower body strapped to a fixed jig, upper torso (top of head to ~T12) strapped in a 'floating' cradle on precision nylon ball bearings over glass (no resistance to planar translation/rotation); scissor jacks aligned the spine in neutral, foam cushions under waist/knees when needed. Bending moment applied to the cradle by a cable kept normal to the cradle (load cell); moment = force x perpendicular distance to the lateral iliac crest (~L4/L5). Axial rotation: upright standing, rib cage fixed by a restraining harness, torque applied to a rotating platform under the feet. Angle = rib cage (3-SPACE Isotrak sensor over xiphoid) relative to pelvis (source strapped to pelvis), accuracy +-0.3 deg. Audio EMG biofeedback (bilateral L3 erector spinae and external oblique) to relax; trials with prolonged EMG repeated. Torque ramped over ~10 s (peak at 7-8 s) until the subject's tolerance limit. 3 trials x 6 directions (flexion, extension, CW twist, CCW twist, right and left lateral bend) x 3 conditions (normal, held breath at maximal inhalation, leather lifting belt 11 cm posterior / 6.5 cm anterior); condition order fixed (normal, breath hold, belt). Mean raw torque-angle data per sex, direction and condition fitted with T = lambda*exp(beta*alpha) (T in Nm, alpha in deg) from 0 Nm up to the torque still tolerated by half the subjects.
how_to_simulate: Same posture and boundary conditions as the normal-condition test (relaxed_trunk_moment_angle_fit)

Belt: add an abdominal belt / hoop stiffness around the abdomen (leather belt 11 cm wide posteriorly, 6.5 cm anteriorly, snug); held breath: add raised intra-abdominal pressure / inflated rib cage at maximal inhalation
Zero muscle activation; compute the passive moment about L4/L5 vs angle and compare with the fit for the same sex, direction and condition
Main check is the direction of the effect: stiffer in lateral bend and axial twist, no change in flexion (and extension except males with held breath)

subject_model.source: Table 1 male means (female cohort: 20.8 y, 164.8 cm, 62.3 kg)

protocol.notes: Belt and breath-hold trials always followed the normal trials (order not randomised). Breath-hold volume not standardised. Some females could not tighten the belt sufficiently. Not strictly passive tissue only (IAP / belt contribute); use for model features that include IAP or bracing devices.

extraction.uncertainty: coefficients as printed (2 decimals); Table 2 X positions read by column alignment, +-1 cell possible
extraction.check_notes: Scanned PDF: Table 3 read from a 300 dpi render (male extension belt lambda printed as '1.5'). Table 2 summarised to torque ranges per column; text confirms: no effect in flexion, extension stiffer only with held breath in males, belt stiffer in lateral bend for both sexes, belt and held breath stiffer in twist except females holding breath in CCW.

pass_rule.rule: model torque within +-25% of the fitted curve for the same sex/direction/condition; sign of the belt or held-breath effect vs normal matches Table 2 (stiffening in lateral bend and twist, none in flexion)
